sentences.en: He kept the Marxist books in his room, took them to the library for renewal, carried them back home.
sentences.zh: 他在房间里藏着马克思主义的书籍，把它们带到图书馆续借，又把它们搬回家。

sentences.en: The books themselves were secret, forbidden and hard to read.
sentences.zh: 这些书本身是秘密的、被禁的，而且很难读懂。

sentences.en: They altered the room, charged it with meaning.
sentences.zh: 它们改变了那个房间，为它注入了意义。

sentences.en: The drabness of his surroundings, his own shabby clothes, were explained and transformed by these books.
sentences.zh: 他周围环境的单调乏味，他自己寒酸的衣着，都被这些书所解释和改变了。

sentences.en: He saw himself as part of something vast and sweeping.
sentences.zh: 他觉得自己是某种宏大而席卷一切的事物的一部分。

sentences.en: He was the product of a sweeping history.
sentences.zh: 他是席卷一切的历史的产物。

sentences.en: He and his mother locked into a process, a system of money and property that diminished their human worth every day, as if by scientific law.
sentences.zh: 他和母亲被锁死在一个进程中，一个金钱与财产的系统里，这系统每天都在贬低他们的尊严，仿佛遵循着某种科学规律。

sentences.en: The books made him part of something.
sentences.zh: 这些书使他成为了某种事物的一部分。

sentences.en: Something led up to his presence in this room, in this particular skin, and something would follow.
sentences.zh: 某种力量引导他来到了这个房间，落入这副皮囊之中，而某种力量也将随之而来。

sentences.en: So that, Dominic, is Don DeLille, the great American novelist, writing about Lee Harvey Oswald in his tremendous novel Libra, which he published in 1988.
sentences.zh: 所以，多米尼克，这是唐·德里罗，伟大的美国小说家，在他1988年出版的巨著《天秤座》中描写李·哈维·奥斯瓦尔德的文字。

sentences.en: And it's actually a while since I read it.
sentences.zh: 而且我读这本书其实已经是前一阵子的事了。

sentences.en: But as I recall, the conspiracy theory in that it's a kind of an alliance of the CIA and Cuban exiles.
sentences.zh: 但据我回忆，其中的阴谋论在某种程度上是中情局和古巴流亡分子的联盟。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They've created a plot because it's a book, not just about the Kennedy assassination, but it's about plotting and narrative, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 他们制造了一个阴谋，因为这本书不仅关乎肯尼迪遇刺，还关乎阴谋和叙事，对吧？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 的确如此。

sentences.en: And it's kind of about the unknowability, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这其实也关乎某种不可知性，对吧？

sentences.en: Because essentially, Don DeLille, who's a brilliantly sophisticated novelist and very aware of the porous borders between fiction and nonfiction,
sentences.zh: 因为从根本上说，唐·德里罗是一位极其老练的小说家，非常清楚虚构与非虚构之间那条模棱两可的界限，

sentences.en: is essentially casting the Warren Commission as another work of fiction.
sentences.zh: 他本质上是将沃伦委员会塑造成了另一部小说作品。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the assassination almost begins as a work of fiction that then comes true, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以刺杀事件几乎是以一部虚构作品开端，然后成真的，不是吗？

sentences.en: They create, the CIA create the conspiracy, they implot it, and then they cast Oswald.
sentences.zh: 他们创造了，中情局创造了这个阴谋，他们筹划了这个情节，然后选中了奥斯瓦尔德。

sentences.en: It becomes true.
sentences.zh: 它成真了。

sentences.en: And then the Warren Commission itself is a kind of narrative.
sentences.zh: 然后沃伦委员会本身也成了一种叙事。

sentences.en: So a little bit like Foucault's Pendulum, Umberto Eco's novel, where a conspiracy theory is constructed and the conspirators find it's actually true.
sentences.zh: 这有点像翁贝托·埃科的小说《傅科摆》，其中构建了一个阴谋论，而阴谋家们发现它竟然是真的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And you can see why novelists have always been fascinated.
sentences.zh: 你可以理解为什么小说家们总是为之着迷。

sentences.en: James Elroy, you mentioned in the last episode, Norman Mailer, I've been fascinated by the Kennedys and the Kennedy assassination, because if you're interested in narrative,
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·埃尔罗伊，你上集提到过，诺曼·梅尔，我都对肯尼迪和肯尼迪遇刺案着迷，因为如果你对叙事感兴趣，

sentences.en: in plotting, as you say, in the relationship between fact and fiction, this is a gift to you as a writer, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，对情节感兴趣，对事实与虚构之间的关系感兴趣，这作为作家简直是天赐的礼物，不是吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: But Don DeLillo places Lee Harvey Oswald, despite all the kind of the wrapping of conspiracy and so on, he places Lee Harvey Oswald at the center of the story,
sentences.zh: 但唐·德里罗把李·哈维·奥斯瓦尔德，抛开所有那些阴谋的外衣等等不谈，他将李·哈维·奥斯瓦尔德置于故事的中心，

sentences.en: rather in the way that actually the Warren Commission does.
sentences.zh: 这其实有点类似于沃伦委员会的做法。

sentences.en: I mean, the Warren Commission says Lee Harvey Oswald did it, and he acted alone, and there was no conspiracy.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，沃伦委员会说李·哈维·奥斯瓦尔德干的，而且他是单独行动，根本没有阴谋。

sentences.en: And Lee Harvey Oswald did not know Jack Ruby, and Jack Ruby, likewise, was not part of a conspiracy.
sentences.zh: 并且李·哈维·奥斯瓦尔德不认识杰克·鲁比，同样地，杰克·鲁比也不是阴谋的一部分。

sentences.en: And we are now, we've done six episodes, I want to know what you think.
sentences.zh: 我们现在已经做了六集节目，我想知道你的看法。

sentences.en: And I'm guessing from pretty much everything that you said beforehand, that you would agree with the Warren Commission, which is great news for the Warren Commission to say.
sentences.zh: 我根据你之前所说的一切推测，你大概会同意沃伦委员会的结论，这对沃伦委员会来说可是个好消息。

sentences.en: It validates them.
sentences.zh: 这证明了他们的正确性。

sentences.en: What a wonderful endorsement for them.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说是多么美妙的肯定啊。

sentences.en: So I think the keys to this crime are in the personality of the victim and of the killer.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这起罪行的关键在于受害者和凶手的性格。

sentences.en: So we spent a lot of time talking about John F.
sentences.zh: 所以我们花了大量时间谈论约翰·F

sentences.en: Kennedy, because I think understanding his personalities was so important to understanding why it's, to me,
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪，因为我认为理解他的个性对于理解为什么在我看来，

sentences.en: inherently implausible that powerful government agencies would wish to murder him in broad daylight.
sentences.zh: 强大的政府机构希望在白昼之下谋杀他，在本质上是难以置信的，这非常重要。

sentences.en: Because I think understanding the essential kind of small C conservatism of Kennedy, his involvement in the Second World War, his devotion to America,
sentences.zh: 因为我认为理解肯尼迪本质上那种小c的保守主义，他参加第二次世界大战的经历，他对美国的忠诚，

sentences.en: his devotion to America's role in the world.
sentences.zh: 他对自己在美国世界角色中的奉献。

sentences.en: When you understand all that, and you understand what kind of president he was, I think that allows you to eliminate some of these suspects,
sentences.zh: 当你理解了这一切，并且理解了他是一个什么样的总统，我认为这能让你排除其中一些嫌疑人，

sentences.en: because it's obvious they would not have any meaningful motive.
sentences.zh: 因为很明显他们没有任何有意义的动机。

sentences.en: But now we come to the man who was seen walking away from the Texas Book Depository and was later involved in shooting the police from J.D.
sentences.zh: 但现在我们来到了那个被看到从德克萨斯教科书仓库走出来，后来又卷入枪杀J.D

sentences.en: Tippett.
sentences.zh: 蒂皮特警官的人。

sentences.en: And I think if we understand Lee Harvey Oswald, Tom, we will understand this crime and we will have the answer to the mystery.
sentences.zh: 并且汤姆，如果我们理解了李·哈维·奥斯瓦尔德，我们就会理解这起罪行，并找到这个谜团的答案。

sentences.en: So you think that Captain Fritz, the man who interrogated him, and who in a sense, I suppose, has a better understanding of what might have motivated him.
sentences.zh: 所以你认为审讯他的弗里茨队长，在某种意义上，我想他对究竟是什么动机驱使了这个人有更好的理解。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And who says that he definitely did it.
sentences.zh: 而且他说这绝对是奥斯瓦尔德干的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You agree with him that it is Lee Harvey Oswald?
sentences.zh: 你同意他的看法，认为凶手就是李·哈维·奥斯瓦尔德吗？

sentences.en: I do, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我同意，汤姆。

sentences.en: I do think Lee Harvey Oswald killed John F.
sentences.zh: 我的确认为李·哈维·奥斯瓦尔德杀害了约翰·F

sentences.en: Kennedy.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪。

sentences.en: And I think when we go into his life and we discuss his movements, it will become clear why he is such a plausible suspect.
sentences.zh: 并且我认为当我们深入他的生活并讨论他的行踪时，就会弄清楚为什么他是一个如此可信的嫌疑人。

sentences.en: And then when we list some of the evidence, you will see that no other explanation carries so much evidentiary weight.
sentences.zh: 然后当我们列举一些证据时，你就会明白没有任何其他解释能承载如此巨大的证据分量。

sentences.en: But let's start with Oswald himself.
sentences.zh: 但让我们从奥斯瓦尔德本人开始说起。

sentences.en: Oswald was born in New Orleans, Louisiana, September 1939, the outbreak of the Second World War in Europe.
sentences.zh: 奥斯瓦尔德于1939年9月出生在路易斯安那州新奥尔良，当时正是欧洲二战爆发之时。

sentences.en: And he is born to Robert Oswald and Margaret Clavery.
sentences.zh: 他的父母是罗伯特·奥斯瓦尔德和玛格丽特·克拉弗里。

sentences.en: It's his mother's second marriage.
sentences.zh: 这是他母亲的第二次婚姻。

sentences.en: His father, Robert, died of a heart attack two months before he was born.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲罗伯特在他出生前两个月死于心脏病发作。

sentences.en: So he is born to a single mother.
sentences.zh: 所以他是单亲妈妈抚养长大的。

sentences.en: His mother is a very, very rackety person.
sentences.zh: 他的母亲是一个非常、非常古怪且让人头疼的人。

sentences.en: She ends up moving to Dallas and he goes to school in Fort Worth initially.
sentences.zh: 她最后搬到了达拉斯，而他最初是在沃斯堡上学。

sentences.en: He is a shy, withdrawn, difficult boy, troubled boy.
sentences.zh: 他是一个害羞、孤僻、难以相处且充满烦恼的男孩。

sentences.en: And this is completely understandable because his mother has married for a third time a guy called Erwin Ekdahl.
sentences.zh: 这完全可以理解，因为他的母亲与一个叫欧文·埃克达尔的家伙进行了第三次婚姻。

sentences.en: And she has a very tempestuous relationship with this guy Ekdahl.
sentences.zh: 她与这个叫埃克达尔的家伙关系非常动荡。

sentences.en: She is a very troubled woman herself, Marguerite.
sentences.zh: 玛格丽特她自己就是一个充满麻烦的女人。

sentences.en: And Lee, you know, like so many children, so many towns across the world, he is affected by that.
sentences.zh: 而李，你知道的，就像世界上许多城镇的许多孩子一样，受到了这种影响。

sentences.en: And, you know, the reports of him that we have at school when he's a little boy are that he is a sullen little boy.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我们掌握的关于他小时候在学校的报告都说他是个闷闷不乐的小男孩。

sentences.en: He's aggressive.
sentences.zh: 他很好斗。

sentences.en: He likes reading.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢读书。

sentences.en: I mean, the reading is we started with books, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，阅读这件事，我们是从书本开始的，汤姆。

sentences.en: And I think the books are important.
sentences.zh: 并且我认为书本很重要。

sentences.en: I think they're really important, actually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我认为它们真的非常重要。

sentences.en: People tend to underestimate the importance of his Marxism and his politics.
sentences.zh: 人们往往低估了他的马克思主义和政治倾向的重要性。

sentences.en: So his mother, you said that she's a kind of a difficult woman, but one of the kind of the keys to her character, it seems,
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是，他的母亲是个挺难缠的女人，但她性格中的关键点之一似乎在于，

sentences.en: is that she feels that her life has not measured up to her expectation of what it should have been.
sentences.zh: 她觉得她的一生远没有达到她所期望的标准。

sentences.en: And do you think that Lee Harvey Oswald has that same sense, a sense of his own talents and the fact that his circumstances are not adequate to those talents?
sentences.zh: 你认为李·哈维·奥斯瓦尔德也有同感吗，觉得自己很有天赋，但现状却配不上这些天赋？

sentences.en: Undoubtedly.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问。

sentences.en: Undoubtedly, Tom.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，汤姆。

sentences.en: So already we have a couple of things that a lot of assassins have in common.
sentences.zh: 所以我们已经发现了很多刺客所共有的几点特征。

sentences.en: So your John Hinckley's, your Arthur Bremmer's, the people who have tried to shoot public figures in American history.
sentences.zh: 比如约翰·欣克利，比如阿瑟·布雷默，那些在美国历史上试图射杀公众人物的人。

sentences.en: It is very common that they will be boys who have had troubled childhoods, who have had very difficult relationships with their parents, who have been lonely, withdrawn, sullen,
sentences.zh: 很常见的情况是，他们都是有着坎坷童年、与父母关系极度恶化、孤独、孤僻、郁郁寡欢的男孩，

sentences.en: but who also have been dreamers.
sentences.zh: 但他们同时也是空想家。

sentences.en: In the same way, you know, that somebody like Adolf Hitler was a dreamer.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道的，像阿道夫·希特勒这样的人就是个空想家。

sentences.en: I mean, if you want to take a much more benevolent, we've mentioned this comparison many times.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你想找一个温和得多的例子，我们已经多次提到过这种对比。

sentences.en: Between Hitler and Churchill.
sentences.zh: 希特勒和丘吉尔之间的对比。

sentences.en: Churchill was also, of course, a dreamer.
sentences.zh: 当然，丘吉尔也曾是个空想家。

sentences.en: Boys tend to be dreamers.
sentences.zh: 男孩子往往都是空想家。

sentences.en: I mean, Churchill's life did measure up to his dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，丘吉尔的人生确实符合了他的梦想。

sentences.en: Hitler made his dreams a reality.
sentences.zh: 而希特勒把他的梦想变成了现实。

sentences.en: Assassins are often boys who continue to have these dreams, but they are constantly disappointed.
sentences.zh: 刺客往往是那些一直怀揣着这些梦想、却不断遭受幻灭的男孩。

sentences.en: Fate and life is against them.
sentences.zh: 命运和生活都在与他们作对。

sentences.en: The odds are against them from the start, and they react to that by being bitter and resentful.
sentences.zh: 逆境从一开始就包围着他们，而他们对此的反应就是满怀怨恨与苦涩。

sentences.en: And that's definitely the case with Lee.
sentences.zh: 李的情况绝对就是这样。

sentences.en: And so, in a sense, they become conspiracy theorists, because they come to feel that life, some malevolent force, whether it's supernatural or not, is acting against them.
sentences.zh: 因此，从某种意义上说，他们成了阴谋论者，因为他们开始觉得生活、某种恶意的力量（无论是超自然与否）正在与他们作对。

sentences.en: Undoubtedly, Tom.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，汤姆。

sentences.en: Undoubtedly.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问。

sentences.en: Lee moves to New York when he's 12 with his mother.
sentences.zh: 李12岁时和母亲一起搬到了纽约。

sentences.en: You know, she's moving around, so it's a very unstable life they lead.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她总是搬来搬去，所以他们过着非常动荡的生活。

sentences.en: Don DeLillo's book that you quoted from at the beginning, that begins with him in New York,
sentences.zh: 你开头引用的唐·德里罗的书，就是从他在纽约开始写起的，

sentences.en: riding the subway trains, overwhelmed by the light and the darkness and the kind of sensory overload of being in New York in the 1950s.
sentences.zh: 他坐着地铁，被光芒与黑暗所淹没，体验着1950年代身处纽约的那种感官过载。

sentences.en: Lee goes to school in the Bronx.
sentences.zh: 李在布朗克斯上学。

sentences.en: He plays truant from school.
sentences.zh: 他逃学。

sentences.en: He is, at this point, identified as a very difficult and troubled boy.
sentences.zh: 在这个时候，他被认为是一个非常难管教且充满心理问题的男孩。

sentences.en: He's sent to a reformatory for a psychiatric assessment.
sentences.zh: 他被送进一所少管所接受精神评估。

sentences.en: And we have a report on him from a caseworker at Columbia University.
sentences.zh: 我们有一份来自哥伦比亚大学社工的关于他的报告。

sentences.en: She says he's detached.
sentences.zh: 她说他很冷漠。

sentences.en: She's withdrawn.
sentences.zh: 他很孤僻。

sentences.en: She quite likes him.
sentences.zh: 她其实挺喜欢他的。

sentences.en: She says there's a rather pleasant, appealing quality about this emotionally starved, affectionless youngster, which grows as one speaks to him.
sentences.zh: 她说在这个情感匮乏、缺乏温情的年轻人身上，有一种相当讨人喜欢、引人注目的特质，随着与他交谈，这种感觉会越来越明显。

sentences.en: And it seems clear that he's detached himself from the world around him because no one in it ever met any of his needs for love.
sentences.zh: 很显然，他将自己从周围的世界中隔绝开来，因为这里没有一个人能满足他对爱的需求。

sentences.en: You know, his mother is totally self-absorbed, crazy affairs and relationships, very difficult, and she doesn't take any interest in Lee.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他的母亲完全以自我为中心，有着疯狂的风流韵事和混乱的关系，极其难缠，而且她根本不关心李。

sentences.en: We also have the report of a psychiatrist from the reformatory guy called Dr. Hartogs, a tense and withdrawn and evasive boy.
sentences.zh: 我们还有少管所一位精神病医生的报告，那个人叫哈托格斯博士，说他是一个紧张、孤僻且爱逃避的男孩。

sentences.en: He likes to give the impression he didn't care about others, difficult to penetrate the emotional wall behind which this boy hides, his feelings of awkwardness and insecurity.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢给人一种不在乎别人的印象，很难穿透这个男孩用来隐藏其笨拙和不安全感的情感壁垒。

sentences.en: He diagnoses him as having personality pattern disturbance with schizoid features and passive aggressive tendencies.
sentences.zh: 他诊断他患有人格模式障碍，具有分裂样特征和被动攻击倾向。

sentences.en: The reason I say all this is, do you remember Captain Fritz's interrogation of Oswald and
sentences.zh: 我之所以说这么多，是因为你还记得弗里茨队长对奥斯瓦尔德的审讯吗，还有

sentences.en: the reaction of all the Dallas PD who said they found Oswald oddly, sometimes detached, robotic, like he wasn't really there.
sentences.zh: 达拉斯警察局所有人的反应，他们说发现奥斯瓦尔德有时表现得奇怪地冷漠、像机器人一样，仿佛他根本不在现场。

sentences.en: This is precisely the description that is given by these people when Lee Harvey Oswald is in his mid-teens in New York.
sentences.zh: 这正是这些人在李·哈维·奥斯瓦尔德十几岁中期身处纽约时对他的描述。

sentences.en: I mean, it's uncanny how similar they are.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们之间的相似之处简直不可思议。

sentences.en: He still has problems at school in 1953.
sentences.zh: 到1953年，他在学校仍然问题不断。

sentences.en: There's talk of him being put into a home away from his mother.
sentences.zh: 当时有人谈论要把他送进一个远离他母亲的收容所。

sentences.zh: 像达菲这样的人，是我们最宝贵的武器。

sentences.en: Devised as a technically rigorous geopolitical action thriller.
sentences.zh: 被设计成一部技术严谨的地缘政治动作惊悚片。

sentences.en: We have two times friendly key.
sentences.zh: 我们有两个临时密钥。

sentences.en: Where Britain plays its strongest hand.
sentences.zh: 英国最强王牌。

sentences.en: He's the beSt.
sentences.zh: 他最棒。

sentences.en: Against its strongest foe.
sentences.zh: 对阵最强劲敌。

sentences.en: Bear Hunt.
sentences.zh: 熊猎人。

sentences.zh: 现已上线，各大播客平台均可收听。

sentences.en: Hello, welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《历史的剩余》。

sentences.en: We are entering the final segment of this great epic sweep through the story of JSK and his murder.
sentences.zh: 我们正在进入这场关于约翰·F·肯尼迪及其遇刺案的宏大史诗叙事的最后阶段。

sentences.en: And, Dominic, Lee Harvey Oswald is now in situ in Dallas with his Russian wife, Marina.
sentences.zh: 而且，多米尼克，李·哈维·奥斯瓦尔德现在和他的俄罗斯妻子玛丽娜一起在达拉斯安顿下来了。

sentences.en: Their daughter, June.
sentences.zh: 他们的女儿，琼。

sentences.en: What's going on?
sentences.zh: 怎么回事？

sentences.en: So, we're in the middle of 1962.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们正处于1962年中期。

sentences.en: Lee, his great adventure to the Soviet Union has not worked out as he thought.
sentences.zh: 李，他去苏联的伟大冒险并没有像他想象的那样发展。

sentences.en: He works as a sheet metal worker initially in the Dallas-Fort Worth area.
sentences.zh: 他最初在达拉斯-沃斯堡地区做钣金工。

sentences.en: He throws that job up pretty quickly, doesn't like it, leaves.
sentences.zh: 他很快就把那份工作甩了，不喜欢，离开了。

sentences.en: He works in a photo print company as a trainee.
sentences.zh: 他在一家照相冲印公司做实习生。

sentences.en: He's fired from that for being insubordinate and difficult.
sentences.zh: 他因为不服从管教和难以相处而被解雇了。

sentences.en: He is now a very aggressive, sullen, troubled, and truculent young man.
sentences.zh: 他现在是一个非常具有攻击性、阴郁、满腹牢骚且好斗的年轻人。

sentences.en: He's always getting into fights.
sentences.zh: 他总是跟人打架。

sentences.en: He beats his wife, who often has bruises and black eyes.
sentences.zh: 他殴打他的妻子，妻子经常带着瘀伤和黑眼圈。

sentences.en: He's still interested in his communism.
sentences.zh: 他仍然对他的共产主义感兴趣。

sentences.en: He has not lost that faith.
sentences.zh: 他没有失去那种信仰。

sentences.en: But his real passion, which I mean, I probably should have mentioned earlier, but his real passion is for Cuba.
sentences.zh: 但他真正的激情，我的意思是，我可能应该早点提到，但他真正的激情是古巴。

sentences.en: It is Cuba that he romanticizes.
sentences.zh: 正是古巴让他充满了浪漫幻想。

sentences.en: It is, Tom, we know people have done that for decades afterwards.
sentences.zh: 就是这样，汤姆，我们知道几十年来人们一直这样做。

sentences.en: They romanticize Cuba, the Cuban Revolution.
sentences.zh: 他们对古巴、古巴革命充满浪漫幻想。

sentences.en: They see it as exotic, as the underdog story.
sentences.zh: 他们认为它是异域风情的，是弱者的故事。

sentences.en: And does his fascination with Cuba succeed his fascination with Russia?
sentences.zh: 他对古巴的迷恋取代了他对俄罗斯的迷恋吗？

sentences.en: Goes to Russia and it's all miserable and lathes and cold and whatever, empty supermarkets.
sentences.zh: 去了俄罗斯，结果全是一团糟、车床、寒冷之类的一切，空荡荡的超级市场。

sentences.en: And then he starts thinking of Cuba because it's romantic and beards and all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 然后他开始想念古巴，因为那里很浪漫，有胡须和诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: Beards, exactly.
sentences.zh: 胡子，没错。

sentences.en: I do wonder whether it's exactly that.
sentences.zh: 我确实在想这是否正是如此。

sentences.en: He was obviously interested in Cuba from 1959 onwards when the Cuban Revolution happened.
sentences.zh: 从1959年古巴革命爆发开始，他显然就对古巴很感兴趣。

sentences.en: But Cuba looms so large in the American consciousness now.
sentences.zh: 但古巴现在在美国人的意识中占据着如此重要的地位。

sentences.en: You've had the Bay of Pigs invasion.
sentences.zh: 你们经历过猪湾入侵。

sentences.en: You've had the Cuban Missile Crisis.
sentences.zh: 你们经历过古巴导弹危机。

sentences.en: Fidel Castro is always in the news.
sentences.zh: 菲德尔·卡斯特罗总是成为新闻焦点。

sentences.en: Cuba is lovely and warm.
sentences.zh: 古巴可爱而温暖。

sentences.en: Palm trees, rum.
sentences.zh: 棕榈树，朗姆酒。

sentences.en: You know, it's kind of, as you say, it's romantic guerrillas in kind of combat fatigues.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这有点像你说的，穿着迷彩服的浪漫游击队员。

sentences.en: You can absolutely see why a troubled young man who has completely bought into the Marxist theory of history would romanticize Cuba.
sentences.zh: 你完全可以理解为什么一个完全接受了马克思主义历史理论的困惑年轻人会对古巴产生浪漫幻想。

sentences.en: And who is still being dumped on by American capitalism.
sentences.zh: 而且他仍然被美国资本主义踩在脚下。

sentences.en: Yeah, because his life is still rubbish, actually.
sentences.zh: 对，因为实际上他的生活仍然很烂。

sentences.en: It still hasn't really worked out.
sentences.zh: 事情依然没有真正理顺。

sentences.en: We get into 1963.
sentences.zh: 我们来到了1963年。

sentences.en: Here is what we know.
sentences.zh: 以下是我们所知道的。

sentences.en: Now, people have absolutely poured over the details of Oswald's life.
sentences.zh: 现在，人们对奥斯瓦尔德生活的细节进行了极其仔细的钻研。

sentences.en: But these are some of the things that we do know for sure.
sentences.zh: 但这些是我们确实确定的事情之一。

sentences.en: We know, I think, beyond any reasonable doubt that on the 12th of March 1963, he bought this mail order rifle under a false name, A.J.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们有充分的理由确信，在1963年3月12日，他用一个假名A.J.购买了这支邮购步枪。

sentences.en: Heidel.
sentences.zh: 海德尔。

sentences.en: Now, why is Lee Harvey Oswald using a false name, you might say, if he's just an ordinary person and not a secret agent?
sentences.zh: 现在，你可能会说，如果李·哈维·奥斯瓦尔德只是一个普通人而不是特工，他为什么要用假名？

sentences.en: It's because he hates authority.
sentences.zh: 那是因为他痛恨权威。

sentences.en: So, almost instinctively, he doesn't want to give his real name.
sentences.zh: 所以，几乎出于本能，他不想报出自己的真名。

sentences.en: But also, he's a fantasist who thinks he's living in a world of espionage and dark deeds.
sentences.zh: 但同时，他也是一个幻想家，以为自己生活在一个充满间谍活动和阴暗勾当的世界里。

sentences.en: But presumably, also, I mean, if he is thinking about actually using this gun on someone, then he wants to cover his tracks as well, right?
sentences.zh: 但据我推测，我的意思是，如果他真的考虑对某人使用这把枪，那么他也会想要掩盖自己的行踪，对吧？

sentences.en: Possibly.
sentences.zh: 有可能。

sentences.en: But I don't think he's thinking about using it on Kennedy, because he can have no reasonable expectation that he and Kennedy will ever be in the same place at the same time.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他没想过对肯尼迪使用它，因为他没有理由期望他自己和肯尼迪会在同一时间出现在同一个地方。

sentences.en: But doesn't he, before Kennedy, he tries to assassinate this guy, Major General Edwin Walker, who's a segregationist living in Dallas.
sentences.zh: 但他不是吗，在肯尼迪之前，他试图刺杀这个住在达拉斯的种族隔离主义者埃德温·沃克少将。

sentences.en: So, do you think he gets the gun with that in mind?
sentences.zh: 所以，你认为他买枪是出于这个目的吗？

sentences.en: Could well do.
sentences.zh: 很有可能。

sentences.en: Could well do, Tom.
sentences.zh: 很有可能，汤姆。

sentences.en: Edwin Walker, so we've said many times in this series about how in the early 1960s, there is this sort of seething, it's more than an undercurrent, it is a stream.
sentences.zh: 埃德温·沃克，正如我们在本系列中多次说过的那样，在20世纪60年代初，有一种翻滚涌动的暗流，不，这不只是暗流，它是一条河流。

sentences.en: It is a babbling brook of discontent.
sentences.zh: 它是一条充满不满的潺潺小溪。

sentences.en: It's not a babbling brook, surely it's a turbid torrent.
sentences.zh: 这不是潺潺小溪，这肯定是一股浑浊的激流。

sentences.en: A turbid torrent, very good.
sentences.zh: 浑浊的激流，非常好。

sentences.en: It's a turbid torrent.
sentences.zh: 这是一股浑浊的激流。

sentences.en: Yeah, a babbling brook was totally wrong.
sentences.zh: 对，说潺潺小溪完全错了。

sentences.en: Babbling brook is like, you know, when we do a podcast about poetry in Edwardian England.
sentences.zh: 潺潺小溪就像是，你知道的，当我们做一个关于爱德华时代英格兰诗歌的播客时那样。

sentences.en: Wordsworth.
sentences.zh: 华兹华斯。

sentences.en: But it's a turbid torrent of right-wing discontent and kind of conspiracy theories and stuff.
sentences.zh: 但这是一股由右翼不满情绪、各种阴谋论等组成的浑浊激流。

sentences.en: And one of the people stirring this up is this guy, Major General Edwin Walker, who says Kennedy is in bed with, you know, communists and black activists and all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 煽动这一切的人之一就是这个家伙，埃德温·沃克少将，他说肯尼迪与共产主义者、黑人维权人士以及所有这些乌合之众同流合污。

sentences.en: He's very against civil rights.
sentences.zh: 他非常反对民权。

sentences.en: And Oswald has clearly read up on him in all his kind of journals and decides he's going to kill him.
sentences.zh: 奥斯瓦尔德显然在各种期刊上读过关于他的文章，并决定杀了他。

sentences.en: Goes to his house in Dallas.
sentences.zh: 他去了达拉斯的住所。

sentences.en: He shoots Edwin Walker and the bullet hits the, it's the windowsill or something like that, or the window frame.
sentences.zh: 他向埃德温·沃克开枪，子弹击中了，是窗台还是别的什么地方，或者说是窗框。

sentences.en: He had left a note for Marina to say, you know, goodbye.
sentences.zh: 他给玛丽娜留了张便条，你知道的，说再见。

sentences.en: I'm, you'll probably never see me again, thinking he would either be killed or he'll be arrested.
sentences.zh: 我，你可能再也见不到我了，他以为自己要么会被杀，要么会被捕。

sentences.en: But actually he comes home very sheepish and kind of shamefaced because he's tried and failed to shoot Major General Edwin Walker.
sentences.zh: 但实际上他回家时显得非常窘迫和羞愧，因为他试图枪击埃德温·沃克少将却失败了。

sentences.en: Now, if you believe this story and there's no reason to doubt it whatsoever,
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你相信这个故事，而且没有任何理由怀疑它，

sentences.en: then you have to accept that Lee Harvey Oswald is somebody who is already thinking about assassinating public figures and is capable of taking the shot.
sentences.zh: 那么你必须承认，李·哈维·奥斯瓦尔德是一个已经在考虑刺杀公众人物并且有能力开枪的人。

sentences.en: And worth mentioning in that context that, of course, when he, on the 22nd of November, 1963, he takes off his wedding ring and he leaves all his money for Marina, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 在这个背景下值得一提的是，当然，当他在1963年11月22日脱下结婚戒指并将他所有的钱留给玛丽娜时，对吧？

sentences.en: Which he does.
sentences.zh: 他确实这么做了。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly right.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: The Edwin Walker thing hasn't worked out.
sentences.zh: 埃德温·沃克那件事没有成功。

sentences.en: Dominic, can I just ask you, on the Edwin Walker thing, presumably he doesn't get, I mean, nobody fingers him for this because otherwise he wouldn't.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我可以问一下吗，关于埃德温·沃克的事，他大概没有被，我的意思是，没有人把这归咎于他，否则他就不会……

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: And actually Theo is asking exactly the same question.
sentences.zh: 事实上，西奥问的正是同一个问题。

sentences.en: How could he try to shoot a member of the armed forces and try to get away with it?
sentences.zh: 他怎么能企图枪击一名武装部队成员却试图逃脱惩罚呢？

sentences.en: So it's at Walker's home.
sentences.zh: 所以那是在沃克的家里。

sentences.en: Walker is a former member of the armed forces.
sentences.zh: 沃克是武装部队的前成员。

sentences.en: And it's in the dark.
sentences.zh: 而且是在黑暗中。

sentences.en: It's at night.
sentences.zh: 那是在晚上。

sentences.en: He shoots from an alley or something into the house, through the yard, and then he kind of scuttles off.
sentences.zh: 他从一条小巷或类似的地方开枪射入屋里，穿过院子，然后鬼鬼祟祟地溜走了。

sentences.en: So actually, how would you catch him?
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，你怎么能抓到他呢？

sentences.en: He's gone.
sentences.zh: 他已经走了。

sentences.en: And he didn't kill him.
sentences.zh: 而且他没把他杀死。

sentences.en: So there's not a huge investigation into it or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 所以并没有对此展开大规模的调查或类似的事情。

sentences.en: So how do they know that he did it?
sentences.zh: 那么他们怎么知道是他干的呢？

sentences.en: He tells Marina.
sentences.zh: 他告诉了玛丽娜。

sentences.en: I think it's Marina who tells people that this is what Lee said he'd done.
sentences.zh: 我想是玛丽娜告诉别人这就是李说他做过的事。

sentences.en: So anyway, he moves to New Orleans for a bit where he'd been born.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，他搬到了他出生的新奥尔良住了一段时间。

sentences.en: He forms a local branch there of the Fair Play for Cuba Committee, which is a kind of left-wing, you know, let's stick up for Cuba kind of group.
sentences.zh: 他在那里成立了“公平对待古巴委员会”的一个地方分支机构，这是一种左翼的、你知道的，支持古巴的组织。

sentences.en: He's briefly arrested in New Orleans for scuffling with anti-Castro activists.
sentences.zh: 他在新奥尔良因与反卡斯特罗活动人士混战而短暂被捕。

sentences.en: And then in September, there's this very peculiar incident when he takes a bus to Mexico City, across the border,
sentences.zh: 然后在9月，发生了一起非常奇怪的事件，他乘公共汽车前往墨西哥城，跨越边境，

sentences.en: and he goes to the consulates of both Cuba and the USSR to try to get a visa for Cuba.
sentences.zh: 他去了古巴和苏联的领事馆，试图获得去古巴的签证。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So you can't just turn up in Cuba then?
sentences.zh: 所以你不能直接出现在古巴？

sentences.en: No, you need a visa.
sentences.zh: 不，你需要签证。

sentences.en: Well, you need a visa because how are you going to – and there's no train.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你需要签证，因为你将如何——而且没有火车。

sentences.en: How are you going to get there?
sentences.zh: 你打算怎么去那里？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: How are you going to get there?
sentences.zh: 你打算怎么去那里？

sentences.en: No ferry.
sentences.zh: 没有渡轮。

sentences.en: And actually, everybody drags their feet.
sentences.zh: 事实上，每个人都在拖延。

sentences.en: It doesn't happen.
sentences.zh: 事情没有发生。

sentences.en: And eventually, he gives up and he comes back home to Dallas.
sentences.zh: 最终，他放弃了，回到了达拉斯的家中。

sentences.en: At that point, he has no connection whatsoever with the Texas Book Depository.
sentences.zh: 在那时，他与德克萨斯教科书仓库没有任何联系。

sentences.en: But on the 14th of October, 12 days after his return to Dallas, so his wife has been in Irving living with this Quaker woman called Ruth Payne, rooming with her, basically.
sentences.zh: 但在10月14日，在他返回达拉斯12天后，他的妻子一直住在欧文，和一个名叫露丝·佩恩的贵格会妇女住在一起，基本上是租住在一起。

sentences.en: And Ruth Payne says to Lee when he comes to call, oh, there's a job going at the book depository, just taking school books to an elevator, basically.
sentences.zh: 露丝·佩恩对前来拜访的李说，哦，教科书仓库有一份工作，基本上就是把学校的教科书搬到电梯里。

sentences.en: Not a very exciting job, but the kind of job that Lee could do.
sentences.zh: 这不是一份很令人兴奋的工作，但却是李能胜任的那种工作。

sentences.en: But also, Don, just to say that if you see yourself as an intellectual, I mean, that must be very humiliating to be carting textbooks around.
sentences.zh: 但是，唐，我也想说，如果你把自己看作一个知识分子，我的意思是，搬运教科书一定是非常羞辱人的。

sentences.en: So maybe that's further incentivizing him with hostility to the system that has failed to recognize his talents and give him the opportunities that perhaps it should have done.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能进一步加深了他对这个未能认可他的才华并给他应得机会的体制的敌意。

sentences.en: That's perfectly plausible, Tom.
sentences.zh: 这完全合乎情理，汤姆。

sentences.en: By that point, by the way, the FBI in Dallas are well aware of him.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，到那个时候，达拉斯的联邦调查局已经很清楚他的情况了。

sentences.en: You know, he has come to their attention.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他已经引起了他们的注意。

sentences.en: This is a source of great embarrassment to them after the assassination.
sentences.zh: 刺杀事件发生后，这给他们带来了极大的难堪。

sentences.en: They have actually gone and spoken to his wife, Marina, and to the Payne, this couple of Payne's, the Quakers, about him and are kind of looking into him.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上已经去和他的妻子玛丽娜，以及佩恩夫妇、那对贵格会夫妇谈过他的情况，并且正在调查他。

sentences.en: But of course, they don't think he's any big threat.
sentences.zh: 但当然，他们不认为他是什么大威胁。

sentences.en: They don't take him terribly seriously.
sentences.zh: 他们没有把他当回事。

sentences.en: When he finds out they've been doing this and people have been asking questions, he becomes inflamed, you know, furious.
sentences.zh: 当他发现他们一直在这样做并且人们一直在打听时，他变得怒不可遏，你知道的，狂怒不已。

sentences.en: He hates the idea of the authorities checking up on him.
sentences.zh: 他痛恨当局调查他的想法。

sentences.en: But anyway, he's got this job at the Books Depository and for the first few weeks, at least, it kind of goes okay.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，他在教科书仓库找到了这份工作，至少在最初的几周里，情况还算顺利。

sentences.en: He hasn't yet been fired.
sentences.zh: 他还没有被解雇。

sentences.en: On about the 7th and 8th of November, these are the dates, the Dallas papers start to announce that John F.
sentences.zh: 大约在11月7日和8日，就是这些日期，达拉斯的报纸开始报道约翰·F·肯尼迪和他的妻子将访问该市。

sentences.en: Kennedy and his wife will come to the city.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，李·哈维·奥斯瓦尔德绝对不可能知道这一点。

sentences.en: There is no way Lee Harvey Oswald could have known this before this point.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 所以在此之前的一切，在某种程度上都是无关紧要的，因为直到这个时候，

sentences.en: So everything before this point, in a way, is kind of irrelevant because up to this point,
sentences.zh: 李·哈维·奥斯瓦尔德绝不可能期望有机会暗杀肯尼迪。

sentences.en: there was no way that Lee Harvey Oswald could ever expect to have an opportunity to kill Kennedy.

sentences.zh: 我们知道，在周四晚上，也就是谋杀发生的前一晚，他做了一件他从未做过的事，

sentences.zh: 那就是在一个工作日的晚上去欧文拜访玛丽娜，并取走了一个包裹，他后来形容那是窗帘杆。

sentences.en: And the fact that at least some, if not most, forensic experts say the shots did come from that direction and could have come from that direction,
sentences.zh: 而且至少有一些（如果不是大多数的话）法医专家表示，子弹确实来自那个方向，并且完全可能来自那个方向，

sentences.en: that suggests a reasonably plausible case.
sentences.zh: 这表明这是一个相当合理的案件。

sentences.en: We know that Lee Harvey Oswald was the only employee of the Texas Book Depository who at any point said he'd been on the sixth floor.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，李·哈维·奥斯瓦ルド是德克萨斯州书库大楼里唯一一个在任何时候都承认自己去过六楼的员工。

sentences.en: He contradicted himself in the interviews, but at one point he does put himself on the sixth floor.
sentences.zh: 他在审讯中前后矛盾，但在某个时刻他确实把自己置于六楼。

sentences.en: We also know, I think very revealingly, he's the only employee of the building who leaves the building.
sentences.zh: 我们也知道——我觉得这非常说明问题——他是大楼里唯一一个离开大楼的员工。

sentences.en: Everybody else stays.
sentences.zh: 其他所有人都留下了。

sentences.en: He leaves immediately after the shooting.
sentences.zh: 他在枪击发生后立刻离开了。

sentences.en: We know that he then behaves very weirdly.
sentences.zh: 我们知道他的行为随后变得非常怪异。

sentences.en: He gets on a bus, he waits on the bus, the bus is stuck in traffic.
sentences.zh: 他上了公交车，在车上等待，而公交车陷入了交通堵塞。

sentences.en: He then gets off the bus and gets a taxi, which is something that as somebody with very little money, he never, ever, ever did.
sentences.zh: 接着他下了车，叫了一辆出租车——作为一个没什么钱的人，他过去、从来、绝对没有做过这种事。

sentences.en: And then we know he goes home to get his revolver.
sentences.zh: 然后我们知道他回家去拿他的左轮手枪。

sentences.zh: 一个警察把他拦了下来，那是J·D·

sentences.zh: 他开枪打死了蒂普特，无辜的人通常是不会这么做的。

sentences.en: I mean, if a policeman flags you down this afternoon, Tom, I find it implausible that you will shoot him.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，汤姆，如果今天下午一个警察把你拦下来，我觉得你不太可能会枪击他。

sentences.en: Well, unless I suppose just assassinated someone, which hopefully I won't have done.
sentences.zh: 除非我刚刺杀某个人吧，希望我不会这么做。

sentences.en: But just to ask, I mean, what's his plan?
sentences.zh: 但我想问的是，他的计划是什么？

sentences.en: If he has shot Kennedy and he's leaving the book depository, I mean, where is he going?
sentences.zh: 如果他枪杀了肯尼迪并正在离开书库大楼，我的意思是，他要去哪里？

sentences.en: What does he think he's going to do?
sentences.zh: 他觉得自己要做什么？

sentences.en: Why is he getting the revolver?

sentences.zh: 他拿左轮手枪是因为他觉得今天下午可能会发生什么事。

sentences.en: Maybe they'll come for me.
sentences.zh: 也许他们会来抓我。

sentences.en: But where do you think he's planning to go?
sentences.zh: 但你觉得他打算去哪里？

sentences.en: Perhaps he's going to go back to Mexico City, make another attempt to get to Cuba.
sentences.zh: 也许他打算回墨西哥城，再次尝试去古巴。

sentences.en: Right.

sentences.en: Okay.

sentences.zh: 所以这里有一种紧张感，对吧？

sentences.zh: 幻想自己成为所有这些事件戏剧中的主角。

sentences.zh: 这对于一个完全被诬陷的人来说，似乎同样是不大可能做出的举动。

sentences.zh: 同样不太可能的还有他在审讯中冷漠、阴沉的表态。

sentences.en: I mean, the thing that always inflames people, he's very funny.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，最让人恼火的是，他非常幽默。

sentences.en: He's very graceful.
sentences.zh: 他非常优雅。

sentences.en: You can imagine at Harvard, there must have been so many people who hated him because he just seemed so spoiled by fate to have all these qualities.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象在哈佛大学里，一定有很多人恨他，因为他似乎被命运过分宠爱，集所有这些优点于一身。

sentences.en: Lee Harvey Oswald must have driven him mad.
sentences.zh: 李·哈维·奥斯瓦ルド一定被他气疯了。

sentences.en: I mean, the famous, the archetype of this is Herostratus, who, the Greek who burnt down, supposedly, the Temple of Artemis at Ephesus, purely so that he would be remembered.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，最著名的典型代表就是黑罗斯图斯，那个希腊人，据说他烧毁了以弗所的阿耳忒弥斯神庙，纯粹为了让后人记住他。

sentences.en: Do you think there's an element of that?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这里面有没有这种成分？

sentences.en: Yeah, political assassinations, there's always a copycat thing.
sentences.zh: 是的，政治暗杀总有一种争相模仿的效应。

sentences.en: The Lee Harvey Oswald one, of course, is the first, and then lots of people copy him.
sentences.zh: 李·哈维·奥斯瓦ルド的那次当然是开端，然后很多人效仿他。

sentences.en: But the people who copy him are very like him.
sentences.zh: 但效仿他的人和他非常像。

sentences.en: You know, the Travis Bickle, Robert De Niro in Taxi Driver kind of archetype, people who are losers, who feel disappointed that things have gone against them.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，像特拉维斯·比克尔（《出租车司机》里的罗伯特·德尼罗）那种典型人物，那些失意者、对诸事不顺感到失望的人。

sentences.en: His profile, going right back to those first profiles that were written about him as a teenager, fits the kind of person that we know these killers are.
sentences.zh: 他的生平资料，一直追溯到那些在他十几岁时为他写的最初的人物侧写，非常符合我们所知的这类杀手的特征。

sentences.en: You know, people who do this are like Lee Harvey Oswald.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，做这种事的人都跟李·哈维·奥斯瓦ルド是一类人。

sentences.en: If you were looking for somebody to fit the profile, he would be the man.
sentences.zh: 如果你在寻找符合这种画像的人，他就是那个人。

sentences.en: But even if it didn't, I think just on the principle of Occam's razor, that you don't overcomplicate solutions.
sentences.zh: 但即使不是，我想仅凭奥卡姆剃刀原理，即不要把解决方案过度复杂化。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That the simplest, clearest solution is likely to be the correct one.
sentences.zh: 最简单、最清晰的解决方案往往就是正确的解决方案。

sentences.en: And it really does point to Lee Harvey Oswald, because conspiracies complicate things, don't they?
sentences.zh: 而这一切确实指向李·哈维·奥斯瓦ルド，因为阴谋论把事情复杂化了，对吧？

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And people love it for that reason.
sentences.zh: 而人们恰恰因为这个原因而热爱阴谋论。

sentences.en: They love to overcomplicate.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢过度复杂化。

sentences.en: They love to believe that they are in possession of secret knowledge that other people don't have.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢相信自己掌握了别人不知道的秘密知识。

sentences.en: And secret knowledge that not just explains this crime, Tom, because if this is done by the CIA working with the mafia, this unlocks all American political history.
sentences.zh: 而且这种秘密知识不仅能解释这起谋杀案，汤姆，因为如果这是由中情局与黑手党勾结完成的，这就解开了整个美国政治史。

sentences.en: Because you realize that actually a shadowy group of people have been controlling the whole thing, and you know this, and your neighbor doesn't.
sentences.zh: 因为你意识到实际上有一群暗中操控的黑手在掌控一切，而你知道这一点，你的邻居却不知道。

sentences.en: It's so emotionally satisfying.
sentences.zh: 这在情感上太令人满足了。

sentences.en: That's why it fascinates so much.
sentences.zh: 这就是它如此令人着迷的原因。

sentences.en: That's why there have been so many films, so many TV episodes, so many novels.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么会有这么多的电影、这么多的电视剧集、这么多的小说。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But I think it fascinates for another reason as well.
sentences.zh: 但我认为它让人着迷还有另一个原因。

sentences.en: The Kennedy assassination happens at precisely the point when the optimism of the 60s is just about to turn.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪遇刺事件恰好发生在60年代的乐观主义即将发生转折的那个时间点。

sentences.en: So whether it contributes to that, or it obviously does contribute to it, because of course what
sentences.zh: 所以无论它是促成了这一点，还是它显然确实促成了这一点，因为当然在短短几年内发生的事情——这也是为什么我认为加里森案以及吉姆·加里森对新奥尔良克莱·肖的调查，然后是那一波

sentences.en: happens in just a few years, and this is why I think the fact that the Garrison case and the Jim Garrison investigation into Clay Shaw in New Orleans, and then the wave of
sentences.zh: 暗杀纪实书籍，它们发生在1966、1967、1968年绝非巧合，

sentences.en: assassination books, the fact that they happened in 1966, 67, 68, I think it's no coincidence
sentences.zh: 因为那是美国正深陷越南战争和民权运动的时刻，

sentences.en: they happened then, because that's the point at which America is engulfed in the Vietnam War,
sentences.zh: 并且已经被关于法律与秩序、暴乱等种种喧嚣的故事所取代。

sentences.en: and the civil rights movement, it has been overtaken by kind of stories about law and order and rioting and so on.
sentences.zh: 这正是肯尼迪遇刺案的背景。

sentences.en: So it's going a little bit Malcolm X.
sentences.zh: 所以事情变得有点像马尔科姆·X了。

sentences.en: Yes, and the soundtrack is now The Doors rather than, you know, The Beach Boys or whatever.
sentences.zh: 是的，现在的配乐变成了门乐队，而不是海滩男孩之类的。

sentences.en: And the Kennedy assassination has come to serve as this kind of punctuation point.
sentences.zh: 而肯尼迪遇刺事件已经成为了一种标点符号般的存在。

sentences.en: That's why it attracts so much attention.
sentences.zh: 这就是它吸引如此多关注的原因。

sentences.en: And it's also said there have been a number of novels in which people time travel and stop the assassination.
sentences.zh: 而且据说还有不少小说，讲的是人们穿越时空去阻止刺杀。

sentences.en: So Stephen King did one.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬·金就写过一本。

sentences.en: Yes, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: 11, 22, 63, that very weird American way that they organise their dates.
sentences.zh: 11月22日63年，他们那种非常奇怪的日期排列方式。

sentences.en: Apologies to American listeners, but it is odd.
sentences.zh: 向美国听众道个歉，但这确实很奇葩。

sentences.en: But it is poor.
sentences.zh: 但这真的很糟糕。

sentences.en: I mean, that should be the takeaway from this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这应该是我们从中得出的结论。

sentences.en: They need to sort their dating system out.
sentences.zh: 他们需要把他们的日期系统整理一下。

sentences.en: But in that one, I think they, Kennedy saved, and then there's a nuclear war in 1974 or something as a result.
sentences.zh: 但在那本书里，我想他们救了肯尼迪，然后结果1974年左右爆发了核战争之类的。

sentences.en: So, and there are kind of various other ones as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，还有各种各样其他的小说。

sentences.en: That sense that it's the key turning point.
sentences.zh: 那种觉得它是关键转折点的感觉。

sentences.en: Which, of course, it isn't though, Tom.
sentences.zh: 当然，汤姆，其实并不是这样的。

sentences.en: Because had Kennedy lived, he would have faced this dilemma in his second term about whether to stay in Vietnam, to actually commit more troops to Vietnam or whether to leave.
sentences.zh: 因为如果肯尼迪活了下来，他在第二任期内将面临两难抉择：是留在越南，真正向越南增兵，还是离开。

sentences.en: Either way, he would have been criticised.
sentences.zh: 无论哪种选择，他都会受到批评。

sentences.en: Whether he would have left office with his reputation as high seems very unlikely.
sentences.zh: 他卸任时的声誉还能否那么高，看起来非常不可能。

sentences.en: But would he have been able to fix all these problems, you know, civil rights, the economy entering the downturn of the late 60s, early 70s, all of those things, the law and order
sentences.zh: 但他能解决所有这些问题吗，你知道的，民权、进入60年代末70年代初低迷期的经济、所有这些事情，还有法律与秩序

sentences.en: issue anxieties about drugs and college campuses and all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 这个问题、对毒品和大学校园的焦虑以及诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: Would the presence of this one man have fixed that?
sentences.zh: 这个男人的存在能解决这一切吗？

sentences.en: Obviously not.
sentences.zh: 显然不能。

sentences.en: Obviously not.
sentences.zh: 显然不能。

sentences.en: So, Dominic, what you're saying is that after seven episodes, it wasn't really very important.
sentences.zh: 所以，多米尼克，你的意思是经过了七集节目，这其实并不是很重要。

sentences.en: No, I think it's hugely important, actually.
sentences.zh: 不，我觉得其实非常重要。

sentences.en: I think it's because it's a sensational subject and a lot of bonkers people who are interested in it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是因为这是一个耸人听闻的主题，而且有很多痴迷于此的疯狂之人。

sentences.en: Academic historians tend to fight shy of it.
sentences.zh: 学院派历史学家往往对它避之不及。

sentences.en: They don't write books about it for utterly understandable reasons.
sentences.zh: 他们不写关于它的书，这是完全可以理解的原因。

sentences.en: But I think the Kennedy conspiracy stuff has played a pretty big part in the rise of populism and in this kind of paranoid conspiracy theory politics that you have in America.
sentences.zh: 但我认为肯尼迪阴谋论在民粹主义的兴起以及美国那种偏执的阴谋论政治中扮演了相当大的角色。

sentences.en: So, the idea of a deep state, the idea that anybody who challenges it will be kind of rubbed
sentences.zh: 所以，深层政府的概念，任何挑战它的人都会被做掉的

sentences.en: out, the idea that there's this sinister, shadowy cabal, an establishment cabal with links
sentences.zh: 概念，那种认为存在一个阴险、暗中操纵的集团的观念，一个与军工复合体、

sentences.en: to the military-industrial complex, to business, to organised crime, to government agencies,
sentences.zh: 商业、有组织犯罪、政府机构有联系的建制派集团，

sentences.en: that, in the last 10 years or so, has become more and more embedded in the American political mainstream, hasn't it?
sentences.zh: 在过去大约十年里，这个观念在美国政治主流中变得越来越根深蒂固，对吧？

sentences.en: The QAnon stuff.
sentences.zh: QAnon那些东西。

sentences.en: Despite the fact that, as you said, if there was a deep state, you think it would have stepped in by now to sort things out.
sentences.zh: 尽管正如你所说，如果有深层政府，你觉得它早就该介入把事情收拾好了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: But, as we approach the next American presidential election next year, you know, there'll be lots
sentences.zh: 但是，当我们迎来明年下一场美国总统大选时，你知道，会有很多人

sentences.en: of people talking about the deep state more vigorously and kind of fervently than ever.
sentences.zh: 比以往任何时候都更加坚定和狂热地谈论深层政府。

sentences.en: So, the legacy...
sentences.zh: 所以，这份遗产……

sentences.en: I mean, this would have happened even without the Kennedy assassination, because as we said in the last episode, this kind of populist paranoia is deeply embedded in the American
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，即使没有肯尼迪遇刺，这也会发生，因为正如我们在上一集里所说，这种民粹主义的偏执深深植根于美国

sentences.en: political tradition.
sentences.zh: 政治传统中。

sentences.en: But the Kennedy conspiracy stuff seemed to take it to its kind of apotheosis, I think.
sentences.zh: 但肯尼迪的阴谋论似乎把这一点推向了它的顶峰，我认为。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So, well worth having done.
sentences.zh: 所以，这节目做得很值。

sentences.en: Seven episodes on.
sentences.zh: 七集节目下来。

sentences.en: And thank you, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，多米尼克。

sentences.en: It's been absolutely fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这真的绝对引人入胜。

sentences.en: I, like everyone, I kind of had a vague sense of the details, but I've really, really enjoyed the opportunity to get to grips with it and to kind of get on top of the...
sentences.zh: 我和大家一样，对细节只有一种模糊的感觉，但我真的非常非常享受这个机会去深入了解它，并掌握……

sentences.en: just the process of what happened and all the various theories about it.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是事情发展的过程以及关于它的各种理论。

sentences.en: So, thank you so much for guiding me and for guiding everyone else through this extraordinary story.
sentences.zh: 所以，非常感谢你引导我和其他所有人经历这个非凡的故事。

sentences.en: Tom, you've been very tolerant in allowing me to do so much on it.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你非常宽容，允许我讲了这么多。

sentences.en: No, not at all.
sentences.zh: 不，完全没有。

sentences.en: I have found it completely fascinating and I entirely understand why people are obsessed by it.
sentences.zh: 我发现它完全引人入胜，我完全理解为什么人们会对此着迷。

sentences.en: It is an extraordinary story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非凡的故事。

sentences.en: Well, what you're not telling people is that you yourself have fallen down this rabbit hole, haven't you?
sentences.zh: 好吧，你没有告诉大家的是，你自己其实也陷入了这个兔子洞，对吧？

sentences.en: Because you've been watching all kinds of terrible documentaries about it.
sentences.zh: 因为你一直在看各种关于它的糟糕纪录片。

sentences.en: I have, but I'm reassured that I haven't been convinced by any of them.
sentences.zh: 我是看过，但我感到安心的是，我没有被其中任何一部说服。

sentences.en: Because having, first of all, I'd kind of immerse myself in the details of what had actually happened.
sentences.zh: 因为首先，我沉浸在实际发生的事情的细节中。

sentences.en: And so, I can kind of spot where things don't entirely fit.
sentences.zh: 所以我能看出哪些地方并不完全吻合。

sentences.en: Theo, we've seen who Theo thinks it is.
sentences.zh: 西奥，我们已经看到了西奥觉得凶手是谁。

sentences.en: Theo still thinks it's LBJ.
sentences.zh: 西奥还是认为是约翰逊总统（LBJ）。

sentences.en: So, he is a grassy Noel truther.
sentences.zh: 所以他是个“林荫小道阴谋论者”。

sentences.en: And on that bombshell, thank you all very much for listening.
sentences.zh: 伴随着这个重磅炸弹，非常感谢大家的收听。

sentences.en: Thank you, Dominic, and we will be back.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，多米尼克，我们还会回来的。

sentences.en: Thanks very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
